# docs_audit_report — 2026-07-03

## TL;DR (stranger's 30-second take)
The hero is genuinely good — I understand what Carnot does (a "second pair of
eyes" that checks LLM answers) and how to install it inside 10 seconds. But the
moment I look for reasons to trust it, the page fights itself: the license is
stated two different ways, five different AUROC-ish numbers float around an
undefined benchmark called "FoVer," and the hero + blog lead with the project's
own retractions and fabrication-catching. Net: a sharp stranger keeps reading a
little, then hesitates to adopt because they can't tell the license or which
number is real.

## TOP 3 PROBLEMS
1. LICENSE CONTRADICTION — hero badge + meta say "MIT-0", footer says "Apache
   2.0 License". A stranger evaluating adoption cannot answer "can I use this?"
2. AUROC / FoVer NUMBER SOUP — 0.9131, 0.91, 0.90, retracted 0.9857, 0.8947,
   and a "0.125 FoVer baseline" (worse than chance); "FoVer" is never defined
   and is used as both the headline benchmark AND a 0.125 baseline we beat.
3. TRUST-UNDERCUTTING FRAMING — the hero's first prose card and 5 of 7 blog
   posts are about the project catching ITSELF fabricating/retracting ("Repinned
   from v2 0.9857", "Caught Cheating", "Two Retractions"). Honest, but to a
   stranger it reads "this project has a fabrication problem."

## DETAILED FINDINGS

### Bloat
- Word-count bloat is NOT a major issue — bento/result card bodies are all under
  the 120/60-word caps. The bloat is by CARD COUNT and density, below.
- Results grid (#results, lines 517–578) — 12 cards spanning code, FPGA
  hardware, GPU-training speedup, synthetic pilots, and adversarial audits — no
  hierarchy, so a stranger skims none and can't find the ONE headline result.
  Suggest cap ~6 and mark the single headline.
- Test-Time Compute & PREM card (lines 495–501) — not word-long but 100% jargon
  ("dynamic budget controller that scales Test-Time Compute based on
  Process-Reward Energy Model variance… intrinsic motivation for continuous
  self-learning"). Reads like a spec note dropped onto a landing page.

### Internal jargon
- Preprint section (line 584) — "paper-v6" — implies five prior papers; means
  nothing to a stranger. Also "pending operator-initiated upload" and
  "non-operator environment" (lines 591–594) are internal-workflow terms.
- Hero "Recent progress" card (line 312) — "Repinned from v2 0.9857",
  "architecture-only 0.8947", "5-seed dual-condition" — versioning + internal
  provenance jargon in the most prominent card on the page.
- Hero stats (lines 305–307) — "382 Completed milestones", "4,578 Experiment
  runs" — internal vanity metrics; a stranger doesn't know what a "milestone" is
  here and 382 of them reads as churn/bureaucracy. The one meaningful stat
  (0.9131 AUROC) is buried fourth.
- Results cards — "EstimationVerifier" (549), "VeriCoT" (559), "CRANE" (554),
  "CCTU" (451, 574), "PRM-BiasBench" (564), "HalluGuard v3" (569), "k=5
  ensemble" (565) — component names, acronyms, and version numbers, none
  expanded.
- "FoVer" — appears in the stats bar, hero card, results, and preprint but is
  NEVER defined. A stranger cannot tell it's a benchmark dataset.
- Features section (line 497) — "PREM (Process-Reward Energy Model)", "TTC" —
  expanded but still opaque.

### Per-milestone narrative
- Hero "Recent progress" card (lines 309–313) reads like a changelog entry:
  "Repinned from v2 0.9857 after pre-submission adversarial audit."
- Stats bar surfaces "382 Completed milestones" as a headline number — internal
  milestone-counting exposed as a public stat.
- Blog section (lines 682–745): 5 of 7 posts are internal-ops retrospectives —
  "Two Retractions and a Rescue", "Regex in an NTK Costume" (cites
  arXiv:2601.18753 in the teaser), "Five FATAL Findings", "Caught Cheating: 95
  Microseconds on a 30B Model", "Why We Report Two AUROCs Now". This is the
  project's internal integrity drama, not landing-page material.

### Inconsistencies
- License: "MIT-0" (line 7 meta, line 291 hero badge) vs "Apache 2.0 License"
  (line 766 footer). Direct contradiction.
- FoVer AUROC headline 0.9131 (lines 308, 312, 589) vs "0.125 FoVer baseline"
  (line 550) — same named benchmark presented as both a ~0.91 headline and a
  sub-chance 0.125 baseline, with no explanation. Reads as cherry-picking.
- Multiple near-identical metrics with no map: 0.9131, 0.91 (line 530, "publication
  gate"), 0.90 AUC (line 550), 0.9857 retracted (line 312). A stranger cannot
  tell which is THE number.
- Section label "What you can check" (line 415) vs contents: "Research
  operations" (how the project builds itself) and "APIs & portable memory" are
  not things the user checks — they don't fit the "Seven capabilities" framing.
- Result meters are internally inconsistent: "+3.0 points" → 14.6% bar (line
  521) but "+4.9 points" → 66.7% bar (526); "0.0pp accuracy delta" → a nearly
  full 95.6% GREEN bar (570). The bars encode nothing consistent and the 0.0pp
  green bar is actively misleading.

### Missing essentials
- LICENSE is unanswerable due to the MIT-0/Apache-2.0 contradiction — this is
  the single most important missing essential for an adoption decision.
- "FoVer" (the headline benchmark) is never defined for a stranger.
- Maintainer is a lone name ("© 2026 Ian Blenke", line 766) — fine, but a
  stranger sees a solo project with no team/backing signal.

### Fabrication signals
- "GSM8K extraction TP rate: 0.5 → 1.0" (line 560) — perfect 1.0.
- "k=5 ensemble catches 60/60 attacks" (line 565) — 100% on n=60.
- "2.0× speedup, identical losses" (line 540) — "identical" is suspiciously
  exact.
- "99.3% of wrong code flagged" on 164 problems (line 431) — very high for
  edge-case detection.
- "Zero false positives" (blog, line 741) — perfect.
- Mitigating anchor exists (the #results intro promises every number is backed
  by a checked-in artifact and labeled by provenance), but the perfect numbers
  above still carry no per-card confidence interval or sample-size note.

### Structural / rendering (worth an operator check)
- The hero "Recent progress" r-card is nested INSIDE the `.stats-bar` flex
  container (lines 304–315) and uses an undefined class `r-desc` (line 312) —
  likely renders as a large card jammed against the four stat numbers, with
  wrong text styling. This is the above-the-fold element.
- The 7th feature card (Test-Time Compute & PREM, line 495) appears to sit
  OUTSIDE the `.bento-grid` that closes at line 494 — likely renders orphaned
  below the grid. Similar stray-`</div>` imbalance around the problem grid
  (lines 346–348). Verify these render as intended.

## WHAT'S WORKING
- The hero one-liner + the 47+28=76 worked example is excellent: a stranger
  understands the product and the problem in one read, jargon-free.
- Install path is immediate and repeated (`pip install carnot-ebm`), and the
  "Extract → Check → Repair" three-card explainer is clean, plain-English, and
  well-scoped.

## RECOMMENDED OPERATOR ACTIONS
1. FIX THE LICENSE CONTRADICTION FIRST — pick MIT-0 or Apache-2.0 and make the
   meta tag, hero badge, and footer agree. This is a hard blocker for adoption.
2. Collapse the AUROC story to ONE headline number with a one-line gloss of what

   Remove or relocate the retracted "0.9857" and the "0.125 baseline" from the
   landing page; move the two-AUROCs nuance to the linked blog post only.
3. Move the "Repinned from v2 0.9857" self-retraction out of the hero card;

4. De-jargon the results cards: expand or drop VeriCoT / CRANE / CCTU /

5. Fix the result meters so bar width tracks the stated metric (and never render

6. Rebalance the blog teasers so the project's own fabrication/retraction

8. Verify the hero r-card nesting and the orphaned 7th feature card actually
